partners.mechanism_chain: ABCC2 (HGNC:147) —DISRUPTS→ Bile acid transport (GO:0015660); ABCC2 (HGNC:147) —DISRUPTS→ Conjugated Bilirubin (CHEBI:17473); Conjugated Bilirubin (CHEBI:17473) —DISRUPTS→ Bile acid transport (GO:0015660); Bile acid transport (GO:0015660) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperbilirubinemia (HP:0002901); SLC16A1 (HGNC:10648) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate transport (GO:0006855); SLC16A1 (HGNC:10648) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate (CHEBI:15361); Lactate (CHEBI:15361) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate transport (GO:0006855); Lactate transport (GO:0006855) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic myopathy (HP:0003700). falsification.text: If functional studies demonstrate that ABCC2 variants associated with Dubin-Johnson syndrome do not impair bile acid transport, or that SLC16A1 variants associated with metabolic myopathy do not affect lactate transport, this hypothesis would be falsified. **Proposed mechanism:** UGT1A1 (HGNC:12580) —PRODUCES→ bilirubin glucuronide (CHEBI:17478); ABCC2 (HGNC:2) —DISRUPTS→ bilirubin glucuronide (CHEBI:17478); UGT1A1 (HGNC:12580) —DISRUPTS→ bilirubin metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-194270); ABCC2 (HGNC:2) —DISRUPTS→ bilirubin metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-194270); bilirubin (CHEBI:17477) —LEADS_TO→ bilirubin metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-194270); bilirubin glucuronide (CHEBI:17478) —LEADS_TO→ unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (HP:0002118); bilirubin glucuronide (CHEBI:17478) —LEADS_TO→ conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (HP:0011324). Mutations in UGT1A1 (Crigler-Najjar type 2) impair the conjugation of bilirubin to bilirubin glucuronide. Mutations in ABCC2 (Dubin-Johnson syndrome) impair the excretion of bilirubin glucuronide. Both defects lead to hyperbilirubinemia, with distinct patterns of unconjugated and conjugated bilirubin accumulation, converging on the central pathway of bilirubin metabolism.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of a common pathogenic variant in ABCC2 or UGT1A1 with a minor allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD would cast doubt on their primary causal roles in these rare diseases. Alternatively, if functional studies demonstrate that ABCC2 and UGT1A1 do not interact or affect the same specific steps in bilirubin metabolism, this proposed overlap would be falsified. _(variant: rs77546948)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of bilirubin metabolism, despite distinct genetic origins and affected steps, could inform therapeutic strategies for hyperbilirubinemia. For instance, interventions targeting bilirubin conjugation or transport could potentially benefit patients with either condition, or highlight the distinct requirements for treatment based on the specific defect.
